correctness.rationale: Pointwise, the induced component count is X−Y+Z, with X the retained vertex count, Y the retained edge count and Z the indicator of full cycle retention. For exchangeable site choices the second moments of X−Y depend on n and the number of incident edge pairs Σ_v binom(d_v,2); Var Z and Cov(X,Z) depend only on n, ℓ and the inclusion probabilities a_j. The only varying term is −2Cov(Y,Z): the two-, one- and zero-cycle-endpoint edges are counted by ℓ, B and n−ℓ−B, respectively, yielding the stated difference. In the quota case the difference vanishes up to ℓ and at the full census, while a_{ℓ+1}−a_{ℓ+2}=a_{ℓ+1}(n−k)/(n−ℓ−1)>0 for the asserted internal interval. At order at most five there are at most two noncycle vertices; in the two-vertex case the two possible attachment types differ in the number of leaves, so cannot be degree-matched. Direct exact enumeration corroborates the exhibited six-vertex pair and its moments.
residual_risks: The witness checks do not establish the all-order formula on their own. The theorem is restricted to the stated matched unicyclic hosts and retention protocols.

evidence: Given the number retained in a Bernoulli sample, the retained set is a uniform fixed-quota sample. The all-p mean is the degree-n Bernstein expansion of the quota means. The two graphs' means agree for all p, so uniqueness makes their quota means agree at each k. Total variance then makes the all-p variance gap the Bernstein expansion of the quota gaps.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For 0≤j≤n, the binomial identity p^j=Σ_k binom(n,k)p^k(1−p)^(n−k)·binom(k,j)/binom(n,j) gives the quota coefficients a_j. The known gap −2ΔB(p^(ℓ+1)−p^(ℓ+2)) therefore has coefficients −2ΔB(a_{ℓ+1}−a_{ℓ+2}); the known mean similarly gives k−na_2+a_ℓ. When ΔB≠0 there must be at least two noncycle vertices; when ΔB=0 the variance comparison is identically zero by uniqueness. The exact positive-coefficient range and the quoted quota values follow, so no distinct valuable quota remainder survives.
